--- title: "Paired tests for the forecasting benchmark: Wilcoxon signed-rank beside Diebold-Mariano-HLN" description: "The twelve forecast cells and, when the committed tables contain them, the Wilcoxon signed-rank p-values and the Benjamini-Hochberg pairwise screen. This page reads only those tables." date: 2026-11-04 date-format: "DD/MM/YYYY" jupyter: python3 --- **Status:** display for the VAT collection forecast manuscript. This page reads the committed comparison tables. It does not read saved forecasts, and it does not refit a model. **Anchor:** `#lab-ben-wsr` (section 4.6 of the single lab page). The manuscript cites this section. The rank stays test sMAPE. The signed-rank test is a robustness check beside the Diebold-Mariano test with the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold correction. It does not replace that test or the model confidence set. ## What is compared The loss is the per-period sMAPE summand. The differential is the loss of the first series minus the loss of the second. A negative median favours the first series. Two reports use that differential. 1. **Leader against the seasonal naive.** One two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test per cell, on the same finite pairs as the Diebold-Mariano test. This p-value is not adjusted for the number of cells. In `comparison.csv` it is `wsr_p`, beside `dm_p`. 2. **Every unordered pair in the cell.** The family is the cell. Adjusted p-values use `statsmodels.stats.multitest.multipletests(..., method="fdr_bh")`, the same call as `lab/paper_eda/_prelude.py`. The rows are in `pairwise_wilcoxon.csv` (`p_raw`, `p_bh`). The signed-rank call is `scipy.stats.wilcoxon(diff, zero_method="wilcox", alternative="two-sided", method="auto")`. All-zero differentials are a tie and do not raise. The code is `wilcoxon_paired` and `pairwise_wilcoxon` in `projects/monitoramento/scripts/forecast_compare.py`. The references are Wilcoxon (1945), DOI `10.2307/3001968`, and Benjamini and Hochberg (1995), DOI `10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x`. ## What the test assumes The signed-rank test assumes independent differentials, symmetric about the median. Forecast errors can be autocorrelated. The Diebold-Mariano correction in this project is the one-step factor. That factor does not remove the dependence from the rank test. A month has 12 test points and a week has 13. Power is low on those grains. Two calls agree at 5 percent when both p-values are below 0.05 or both are not. Agreement is a call on the seasonal naive. It is not a claim that the leader beats every rival. The two calls do not agree in every cell. ## The twelve cells ::: {#tbl-cells .cell tbl-cap='Twelve cells from the committed comparison table. Series and grain identify each row. Wilcoxon columns appear when comparison.csv contains them. Agree at 5 percent means the Diebold-Mariano and Wilcoxon calls are on the same side of 0.05.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

The heatmap is one cell at a time. The mark is the adjusted p-value. Darker is smaller. Read a cell against its own scale. Do not treat a dark cell as a new rank, and do not compare shades across cells. In `pairwise_wilcoxon.csv`, a count of non-zero differentials equal to 1, 2, 3, or 4 is blank. ``` ::: ::: ## What this page does not conclude A dark cell is not a published winner. A disagreement between the two tests on a month or a week is expected when the test block is short. The reading of those disagreements for the manuscript is left to the authors. The Diebold-Mariano-HLN call and the Wilcoxon call disagree at 5 percent in 2 of the 12 cells. For declared debt on a month, the HLN p-value is 0.040 and the Wilcoxon p-value is 0.064. For declared debt on a calendar day, the HLN p-value is 0.069 and the Wilcoxon p-value is 0.026. The two calls do not agree in every cell.
